# Arkiv Chain Indexer

This repository contains a Bun and TypeScript Ethereum block scanner, PostgreSQL storage layer,
range/sender aggregators, HTTP backend, Baseload worker control plane, Redis-backed recent-sender
leaderboards, and a static frontend.

The backend API is implemented in `src/server.ts` and started by `bun run serve` through
`src/serve.ts`. It serves stored scanner data from PostgreSQL only. It does not fetch blocks from
JSON-RPC during normal API requests. The production frontend serves the React app and proxies
requests with the `/api/` prefix to the backend after stripping `/api`; the backend paths below are
the direct unprefixed paths.

## Core Runtime Commands

```sh
bun install
bun test
DATABASE_URL=postgres://gas:gas@localhost:5432/gas bun run serve
DATABASE_URL=postgres://gas:gas@localhost:5432/gas bun run aggregate -- --range 50
DATABASE_URL=postgres://gas:gas@localhost:5432/gas bun run aggregate-all -- --once
DATABASE_URL=postgres://gas:gas@localhost:5432/gas bun run aggregate-senders -- --once
docker compose up --build
```

## Backend Configuration

`bun run serve` accepts CLI flags and environment variables:

| CLI flag | Environment variables | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--database-url <url>` | `DATABASE_URL`, `SCANNER_DATABASE_URL` | required | PostgreSQL connection string. |
| `--port <port>` | `SERVER_PORT` | `3000` | Backend TCP port. Use `0` for any free port. |
| `--host <host>` | `SERVER_HOSTNAME` | Bun default | Interface/hostname to bind. |
| `--transaction-data-enabled <bool>` | `SERVER_TRANSACTION_DATA_ENABLED`, `SAVE_TRANSACTION_DATA` | `true` | Enables transaction inspection endpoints and advertises transaction features in `/health`. |
| `--baseload-admin-bearer-token <token>` | `BASELOAD_ADMIN_BEARER_TOKEN` | unset | Optional bearer token for mutating Baseload requests and saved config routes. |
| `--baseload-initial-config <path>` | `BASELOAD_INITIAL_CONFIG_PATH` | unset | Optional Baseload worker config JSON file loaded once at backend startup. |
| `--redis-url <url>` | `REDIS_URL`, `SERVER_REDIS_URL` | unset | Enables Redis-backed `/guzzlers` and `/guzzler/:address` APIs. |

Related scanner and worker settings:

- `SAVE_TRANSACTION_DATA=true` or `SCANNER_SAVE_TRANSACTION_DATA=true` makes the scanner persist
  transaction rows. Without stored transaction rows, transaction endpoints may be enabled but have no
  useful data.
- `DECODER_URL` or `SCANNER_DECODER_URL` points to the Arkiv transaction decoder. It is used only
  when transaction data is stored.
- `BASELOAD_RPC_NODE` enables backend Baseload workers to submit Arkiv operations.
- `BASELOAD_MNEMONIC` or `MNEMONIC` controls backend Baseload wallet derivation. If unset, a
  deterministic development mnemonic is used.
- `BASELOAD_PAYLOAD_PROVIDER_URL` configures the payload provider used by Baseload create/update
  operations. Optional related settings are `BASELOAD_PAYLOAD_PROVIDER_BEARER_KEY`,
  `BASELOAD_PAYLOAD_PROVIDER_NAMESPACE` (default `arkiv.entities`), and
  `BASELOAD_PAYLOAD_PROVIDER_VERIFY_RECEIPT` (default `true`).

## Global API Conventions

- All responses include permissive CORS headers.
- `OPTIONS` to any path returns `204`.
- Unsupported methods return JSON errors: `{ "error": "..." }`.
- Unknown paths return `404` with `{ "error": "Not found: /path" }`.
- Most route validation errors return `400`.
- Mutating Baseload routes may return `401` for missing bearer tokens or `403` for invalid bearer
  tokens.
- The backend never returns raw transaction calldata and never stores decoded Arkiv payload bytes.
  It stores and returns payload size only.
- Wei, gas, nonce, block number, and other values that may exceed JavaScript precision are returned
  as decimal strings unless a response type is explicitly a small number.
- Dates are ISO-8601 UTC strings.
- `order` parameters accept `asc` or `desc`; invalid values return `400`.
- Integer query parameters must be non-negative or positive as required by the route.
- `/blocks`, `/ranges`, `/transactions`, `/transaction-records`, `/senders`, and `/guzzlers`
  compress their JSON when the request `Accept-Encoding` header allows it: `zstd` is preferred and
  `gzip` is the fallback, reported in `Content-Encoding` with `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. Clients that
  accept neither get normal JSON. gzip matters behind a CDN or reverse proxy, which commonly asks
  the origin for gzip only and re-encodes for the browser.
- List endpoints return compact rows: a `names` array states the field order once and every row is
  a JSON array of values in that order, so field names are not repeated per row.
- `/blocks` and `/ranges` responses are cached in memory per query string and encoding
  (`LIST_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`, default 200; `LIST_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, default 64 MiB;
  `LIST_CACHE_TTL_MS`, default 5 s; any set to 0 disables caching). The cache is cleared the moment
  a block is committed, so responses can trail a new block only briefly if that notification drops.
- `/transactions` caches its `totalCount`/`totalPages` total per filter, so every page of one query
  shares a single `COUNT(*)` (`TRANSACTION_COUNT_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`, default 500;
  `TRANSACTION_COUNT_CACHE_TTL_MS`, default 5 s; either set to 0 disables caching). It is cleared on
  block commit alongside the list cache, so a total can trail a new block only briefly.

## Feature Gates

| Feature | Enabled by | Affected endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transaction inspection | `SERVER_TRANSACTION_DATA_ENABLED` or `SAVE_TRANSACTION_DATA` not false | `/block/:blockNumber`, `/transactions`, `/transaction/:hash`, `/entity/:entityKey`, `/senders` return `404` when disabled. |
| Transaction records | Stored transaction record rows | `/transaction-records` remains routed even if transaction data is disabled, but it is useful only with record data. |
| Arkiv operation metadata | Scanner transaction storage plus decoder URL | `/transactions` may include `operationsSummary`; `/transaction/:hash` includes `operations`. |
| Baseload workers | Backend started with Baseload runtime; `BASELOAD_RPC_NODE` required to actually submit transactions | `/baseload` status is public; runtime-dependent writes fail if runtime is unavailable. |
| Baseload admin protection | `BASELOAD_ADMIN_BEARER_TOKEN` | Mutating `/baseload`, all `/baseload/configs...`, and `/admin/verify`. |
| Guzzlers | `REDIS_URL` or `SERVER_REDIS_URL` | `/guzzlers` and `/guzzler/:address`; disabled routes return `503`. |
| JSON-RPC | Always on; `features.jsonRpc` in `/health` | `POST /shadow-rpc`. Transaction-backed methods answer JSON-RPC error `-32000` when transaction data is disabled. |
| Account balances | `SCANNER_TRACK_BALANCES` on the scanner; `account_balances` rows | `GET /balances` and `eth_getBalance` on `/shadow-rpc`. Both answer empty/`-32000` without stored readings. |
| JSON-RPC passthrough | `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM`; forwarded methods listed in `features.jsonRpcPassthrough` in `/health` | Relays only the listed methods (`eth_sendRawTransaction` and the `arkiv_*` entity reads by default) to a real node. Unset, they answer `-32601`. |
| Entity query index (experimental) | `ENTITY_QUERY_INDEX=true`; status in `features.entityQueryIndex` in `/health` | `POST /shadow-rpc/experimental` answers `arkiv_query`, `arkiv_getEntity`, `arkiv_getEntityCount`, `arkiv_getBlockTiming` from the indexer's own entity tables. `404` when off. |

## Endpoint Index

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OPTIONS` | any | CORS preflight. |
| `GET` | `/health` | Backend, scanner, database, feature, and guzzler cache health. |
| `GET` | `/sync` | Scanner lag versus the chain head, catch-up trend, and sync ETA. |
| `POST` | `/shadow-rpc` | Ethereum JSON-RPC 2.0 served from stored data, plus any methods the optional passthrough relays to a real node. |
| `GET` | `/blocks` | Compact rows for stored per-block metrics. |
| `GET` | `/blocks/:blockNumber` | One compact stored block row. |
| `GET` | `/block/:blockNumber` | Stored block plus stored transaction rows for inspection. |
| `GET` | `/ranges` | Compact rows for precomputed fixed-size block ranges. |
| `GET` | `/transactions` | Stored transaction rows with pagination and filters. |
| `GET` | `/transaction/:hash` | One stored transaction plus decoded Arkiv operations. |
| `GET` | `/entity/:entityKey` | Most recent stored operations for one Arkiv entity key, with the total count. |
| `GET` | `/transaction-records` | Top stored transaction records by gas, fee, and effective fee. |
| `GET` | `/senders` | Precomputed sender-address activity stats. |
| `GET` | `/balances` | Account balance readings per block, for addresses a block touched. |
| `GET` | `/guzzlers` | Redis-cached active sender leaderboards over recent windows. |
| `GET` | `/guzzler/:address` | One sender's recent per-minute guzzler history. |
| `GET` | `/baseload` | Current backend Baseload state and worker statuses. |
| `PUT` | `/baseload` | Replace Baseload worker config and reconcile workers. |
| `GET` | `/admin/verify` | Validate the configured Baseload admin bearer token. |
| `GET` | `/baseload/configs` | List saved Baseload configs. |
| `GET` | `/baseload/configs/:name` | Fetch one saved Baseload config. |
| `PUT` | `/baseload/configs/:name` | Save or replace one named Baseload config. |
| `DELETE` | `/baseload/configs/:name` | Delete one named Baseload config. |
| `PUT` | `/baseload/configs/:name/load` | Load one saved config into the active Baseload runtime. |

## `GET /health`

Returns:

- `ok`: boolean.
- `serverTimeUtc`: current server timestamp.
- `build`: build metadata from `src/buildInfo.ts`.
- `scanner`: progress fields:
  `lastSuccessfulBlock`, `lastSuccessfulBlockDate`, `lastSuccessfulScannedAtUtc`,
  `lastBlockAgeSeconds`, `backfillNextBlock`, `latestObservedBlock`, `safeHeadBlock`,
  `latestObservedAtUtc`, `latestObservationAgeSeconds`, `headLagBlocks`, `safeHeadLagBlocks`.
- `database`: `totalSizeBytes` plus per-table `tableName`, `rowCount`, `tableSizeBytes`,
  `indexesSizeBytes`, `totalSizeBytes`. `rowCount` is the Postgres planner estimate
  (exact counts would scan every table on each call), so it can trail the true count
  slightly between autovacuum analyzes.
- `features`: booleans for `transactionData`, `guzzlers`, and `jsonRpc`.
- `guzzlers`: Redis cache health: `enabled`, `entryCount`, `bucketCount`, `oldestBucket`,
  `newestBucket`, `totalSizeBytes`.
- `sync`: the same object served by `GET /sync`.

## `GET /sync`

Reports how far the forward scanner is behind the chain head and whether it is closing the gap.
Served from an actively precomputed in-memory body — recomputed immediately after every stored
block and on a periodic refresh (`SYNC_REFRESH_MS`, default 5 s) — so polling it costs the backend
no database work. `serverTimeUtc` is the time of the last recompute, at most a few seconds old.

Returns `ok`, `serverTimeUtc`, and `sync` with:

- `state`: `synced`, `catching-up`, `holding`, `falling-behind`, `stalled`, or `unknown`.
- `summary`: one-line human-readable status.
- `lagBlocks` / `lagSeconds`: distance to the estimated chain head, in blocks and in chain time.
- `observedLagBlocks`: distance to the last head the scanner actually observed.
- `estimatedHeadBlock`, `latestObservedBlock`, `latestObservedAtUtc`, `headObservationAgeSeconds`,
  `headObservationStale`: chain head observation and its extrapolation to now.
- `scanBlocksPerSecond`, `chainBlocksPerSecond`, `chainBlockTimeSeconds`, `speedupFactor`,
  `netCatchUpBlocksPerSecond`: measured throughput and trend.
- `etaSeconds` / `etaUtc`: projected time to be in sync; `null` unless the state is `catching-up`.
- `measuredBlocks`, `measuredWindowSeconds`: the sample window the rates were measured over.

## `POST /shadow-rpc`

An Ethereum JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint answered from stored scanner data. No read ever reaches a node; the one
exception is the optional passthrough below, which relays transaction submission to a real one because no
index can accept a transaction. Single requests and batches (up to 100 entries, 1 MiB body) are accepted; every reply is
HTTP `200` with a JSON-RPC body, including errors, so standard clients (`viem`, `ethers`, `cast`) can point at
`/shadow-rpc` (or `/api/shadow-rpc` through the frontend proxy and nginx) directly. `GET /health` advertises it
under `features.jsonRpc`.

The name is a warning, not decoration: this is a *shadow* of the chain cast by the index, not a node. It
answers from what the scanner happened to store, so treat it as a fast read cache for indexed history rather
than a source of truth — anything you would trust for consensus, settlement or proofs belongs on a real node.
Two differences in particular are deliberate:

- **`latest` means the indexed head.** `eth_blockNumber` and the `latest` / `pending` / `safe` / `finalized`
  tags all resolve to `scanner_state.last_successful_block`, not the chain head. `eth_syncing` reports the gap
  (`false` once the scanner is within a few blocks of the observed head). `earliest` is the oldest stored block.
- **Fields the scanner does not persist are `null`.** Block, transaction and receipt objects keep the standard
  shape, but roots, miner, `logsBloom` and signatures (`v`/`r`/`s`) come back as `null` until those are
  indexed. `input` is always `null`: calldata is never stored. Block `hash` / `parentHash` (and the `blockHash`
  on transactions, receipts and logs) plus receipt event logs (`transaction_logs`: address, topics, data) are
  stored for every block scanned since those columns were added; blocks scanned before that keep `null` (there
  is no backfill) — hash-addressed lookups of those answer `null` like a node does for an unknown hash, and
  their receipts report `logs: null` rather than `[]` so "not indexed" is distinguishable from "no events".

Transaction counts and listings only cover stored rows — the scanner drops the chain's system transaction
(sender `0xDeaD…0001`), so a block's `transactions` array and `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber` are one
lower than a node reports on blocks that carry it; `transactionIndex` keeps the original on-chain position.

| Method | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `web3_clientVersion` | `arkiv-chain-indexer/v<version>[-<commit>]/bun-<version>`. |
| `eth_chainId`, `net_version` | Chain id the scanner persisted at startup (`-32000` until it has). |
| `net_listening`, `eth_mining`, `eth_hashrate`, `eth_accounts` | `true`, `false`, `0x0`, `[]`. |
| `eth_blockNumber` | Indexed head. |
| `eth_syncing` | `false`, or `{ startingBlock, currentBlock, highestBlock }` while behind. |
| `eth_getTransactionCount(address, tag)` | Highest stored nonce sent by `address` up to `tag`, plus one (exact for EOAs). |
| `eth_getBalance(address, tag?)` | Newest stored balance reading for `address` at or before `tag` (see `GET /balances`). `-32000` when the index holds no reading that early — never `0x0`. |
| `eth_gasPrice`, `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas` | geth's oracle over stored data: the 60th percentile of each of the last 20 blocks' cheapest tip; `eth_gasPrice` adds the indexed head's base fee. |
| `eth_feeHistory(count, newest, percentiles?)` | Exact: per-block `baseFeePerGas`, `gasUsedRatio`, and gas-weighted `reward` percentiles from stored transactions (max 1,024 blocks). The closing "next block" base fee repeats the newest one when that block is not stored yet. |
| `eth_getBlockByNumber(tag, full)`, `eth_getBlockByHash(hash, full)` | Stored block; hashes or full transaction objects. `{ "blockHash": … }` block parameters work too. |
| `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber(tag)`, `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash(hash)` | Stored transaction count. |
| `eth_getTransactionByHash`, `eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex`, `eth_getTransactionByBlockHashAndIndex` | Stored transaction object. |
| `eth_getTransactionReceipt(hash)` | Stored receipt fields (`status`, `gasUsed`, `cumulativeGasUsed`, `effectiveGasPrice`, `contractAddress`) and stored `logs` (`null` for pre-logs rows). |
| `eth_getLogs(filter)` | Stored logs matching `fromBlock`/`toBlock` (default `latest`, `toBlock` clamped to the indexed head) or `blockHash`, `address` (one or a list) and positional `topics` (value, list of alternatives, or `null`). At most 10,000 blocks per call and 10,000 matching logs, otherwise error `-32000`. |
| `eth_getUncle*` | No uncles: counts are `0x0`, lookups `null`. |

Transaction-backed methods return `-32000` when transaction data is disabled. Unknown methods return
`-32601`, so state methods (`eth_call`, `eth_estimateGas`, …) fail fast instead of silently hitting a node —
unless the passthrough below is configured to forward them.

### Passthrough to a real node

Everything above is answered from PostgreSQL, which works for reads and cannot work for writes: a transaction
has to reach a node's mempool, and no amount of stored history puts it there. Setting `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM`
opens one narrow hole — the methods in `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM_METHODS`, and only those, are relayed to that node
and their answers returned unchanged. It is never an open proxy. Unset (the default) nothing is forwarded and
the endpoint talks to nothing but PostgreSQL. `GET /health` lists what is forwarded under
`features.jsonRpcPassthrough`, or `false` when nothing is.

| Environment variable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM` | unset | JSON-RPC node forwarded calls are sent to; unset disables the passthrough. In compose, `http://rpc-proxy:8788` reuses the pooled-key proxy. |
| `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM_API_KEY` | unset | Sent as `x-api-key`, for an upstream that wants a header rather than a key baked into the URL. |
| `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM_METHODS` | `eth_sendRawTransaction,arkiv_query,arkiv_getEntity,arkiv_getEntityCount,arkiv_getBlockTiming` | Methods to forward. Each overrides the locally answered one. |
| `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` | `10000` | How long one forwarded call may take. |
| `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `600` | Forwarded calls per minute across all callers; `0` removes the cap. |

Worth knowing before pointing a wallet at it:

- **`eth_sendRawTransaction` is the only write method forwarded by default.** Wallets and SDKs sign locally
  and submit the raw form; `eth_sendTransaction` would need the node to hold keys, which a public endpoint has
  no business relying on. List it explicitly if a deployment's node really does.
- **The Arkiv entity reads (`arkiv_query`, `arkiv_getEntity`, `arkiv_getEntityCount`, `arkiv_getBlockTiming`)
  are forwarded by default too.** The index stores operation metadata, never an entity's live state, so on
  this path nothing but the node answers them. The frontend's `/data` page queries entities through them. The
  experimental entity index below is the opt-in second opinion: the same methods, answered from PostgreSQL,
  on a path of their own.
- **The node's rejection is the answer.** `nonce too low`, `already known`, `insufficient funds` and their
  codes are relayed verbatim; that is the point of forwarding. Failures on our side of the wire (unreachable
  node, non-`200`, malformed reply) answer `-32000` with a fixed message and log the detail server-side,
  because the upstream URL can carry a key.
- **The list is a general escape hatch.** Anything on it is answered by the node whether or not the index
  could have answered it. Adding `eth_call` and `eth_estimateGas` makes the endpoint usable by a wallet;
  adding `eth_getTransactionCount` swaps the indexed nonce — which lags the chain by the scanner's lag — for
  the node's live one, which matters when a sender has transactions the scanner has not reached yet.
- **Forwarded calls are capped as a whole.** A public endpoint fronting a metered node is a way to spend
  someone else's quota, so the rate limit is on by default. It applies across all callers, not per IP.

Example:

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:3000/shadow-rpc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_feeHistory","params":["0x5","latest",[25,50,75]]}'
```

### Experimental: entity reads from the index (`POST /shadow-rpc/experimental`)

Off by default. With `ENTITY_QUERY_INDEX=true` the backend folds the decoded Arkiv operations
(`transaction_operations`, so `SAVE_TRANSACTION_DATA=true` and a `DECODER_URL` are required) and the receipt
event logs (`transaction_logs`) into two tables of its own — `entity_versions`, one row per state an entity
went through with the block range it held for, and `entity_version_attributes`, that state's typed
attributes — and answers `arkiv_query`, `arkiv_getEntity`, `arkiv_getEntityCount` and `arkiv_getBlockTiming`
from them on a **separate path**, `POST /shadow-rpc/experimental` (`/api/shadow-rpc/experimental` publicly).
`/shadow-rpc` is untouched and keeps relaying those methods to the node, so the two paths are two independent
sources for the same questions, and either can be checked against the other. The path answers `404` when the
feature is off; `GET /health` reports it under `features.entityQueryIndex` as `false` or as
`{ path, methods, floorBlock, projectedThroughBlock, lagBlocks, liveEntities, lastFoldAtUtc }`.

The wire contract is the node's (`arkiv-reth-rpc` / `arkiv-rpc-types` in the 0.8 engine): the same parameter
shapes and defaults (`atBlock` hex or `latest`, `limit` 1–200 default 100, `select` with `attributes` as a
boolean or a per-name map), the same query grammar and limits (`*`, `= < <= > >= STARTSWITH`, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`,
typed literals, `$owner $creator $key $expiresAt $createdAt $contentType`; 8 KiB, 64 predicates, depth 32),
the same error codes with the same messages and byte positions (`-32001` malformed, `-32002` type, `-32003`
literal, `-32004` limit, `-32005` cursor, `-32006` block unavailable), the same newest-first order, the same
encodings (`u64`/`createdAt`/`updatedAt`/`expiresAt` as hex, `i32` as a number, `dec` as a trimmed decimal
string, `u256` minimal hex, addresses/keys lowercase), attributes sorted by name, and the same fold semantics:
a patch merges (a tombstone unsets), every mutation bumps `updatedAt`, expiry is the receipt event's value
when logs are stored and the calldata's otherwise, a reverted transaction applies nothing, and an entity is
live at block `B` while `expiresAt > B` and it was not deleted — so a query evaluated `atBlock` a past block
sees exactly what was live then.

Where the index cannot honour something the node does, it says so rather than approximating:

| | Node | Index |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `latest` | The chain head. | The **projection head** (`projectedThroughBlock` in `/health`): the newest block folded, a few blocks behind the scanner head, itself behind the chain. `blockNumber` in every reply says which block answered. |
| History | Any block the node keeps state for. | Blocks between the **floor** and the projection head; anything else is `-32006` with `{ requested, latest }`. The floor is the first block whose stored creates carry entity keys (`floorBlock` in `/health`); entities created before it are unknown, so counts count what the index holds. A backfill that writes older blocks lowers the floor as it goes; `ENTITY_INDEX_FLOOR_BLOCK` pins it instead. |
| `select.payload` | The bytes. | Refused with `-32000`: payload bytes are never stored (the calldata invariant). `arkiv_getEntity` leaves `payload` out. |
| `creationFlags` | Always known. | `null` for entities created before receipt logs were stored (the flags travel in the `EntityCreated` event, not the calldata). |
| Cursors | Resume below an internal entity id. | Resume below a creation position. Both are opaque, bound to the query, block and `select`, and reject a cursor from another request with the node's own messages — but a cursor from one source cannot be handed to the other: the index answers a node's cursor with `-32005` and a message saying so. |
| `arkiv_getBlockTiming` | The node's clock. | The scanner head's block and its timestamp. |

The projection is kept up to date by an in-process projector: every few seconds it folds the operations of the
blocks the scanner has stored since its last pass (per entity key, replaying the key's whole history, so a
refold is idempotent), and once a minute it looks for operation rows written *below* its fold point — a gap
fill, a rescan, the backfill scanner — and refolds those keys too. A first build walks the whole stored
history in chunks and takes minutes for a few hundred thousand blocks. All writes run under an advisory lock,
so two backends on one database never fold on top of each other.

Two scripts turn the pair into a test rig. `scripts/compareEntityQuery.ts --node <url> --index <url>` walks
the same queries on both sides at the same block — discovering them from the data, plus any fixture manifest —
and reports every difference in order, fields, page boundaries, counts, `arkiv_getEntity` and the error
code/message/position of invalid requests, with `--bench` timing both. `scripts/seedEntityQueryFixtures.ts`
creates a suite of entities covering every attribute type, every mutation, expiry, flags and reverting
transactions, and writes the manifest the comparison reads. Point `--node` at the upstream RPC rather than
a public `/shadow-rpc`, whose forwarded-call cap would otherwise pace the run and skew its timings.

The frontend's `/data` page picks its RPC source at the top of the page: the default node
(`/shadow-rpc`), the experimental index (`rpc=index` in shared links), or **both** (`rpc=both`), which
sends each query to the two endpoints at once — pinned to the lower of their two heads so the index's lag
is not read as a difference — and prints the timings side by side with every field the answers disagree on,
the browser-side twin of `scripts/compareEntityQuery.ts`. Only the first page is compared: a cursor belongs
to the endpoint that issued it.

## `GET /blocks`

Returns stored block metric rows. Results default to newest first and are capped at 10,000 rows.
Filters combine additively.

Query parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `blockGt` | Only blocks with `block_number > blockGt`. |
| `blockLt` | Only blocks with `block_number < blockLt`. |
| `dateGt` | Only blocks with `block_date > dateGt`; value is parsed as ISO-8601. |
| `dateLt` | Only blocks with `block_date < dateLt`; value is parsed as ISO-8601. |
| `limit` | Positive integer, maximum 10,000. |
| `order` | `desc` default, or `asc`. |

Response shape:

```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "limit": 10000,
  "truncated": false,
  "filters": {
    "blockGt": null,
    "blockLt": null,
    "dateGt": null,
    "dateLt": null
  },
  "names": ["blockNumber"],
  "blocks": []
}
```

`names` field order:

```txt
blockNumber, blockDate, blockTimeSeconds, baseBlockFeeWei, totalGasUsed, totalInputDataSizeBytes,
totalInputDataCompressedSizeBytes, maxGasInBlock, transactionCount, blockRewardWei,
burntFeesWei, totalTransactionFeeWei, feePriceSumWei, priorityFeeSumWei,
priorityFeeWeightedNumeratorWei, priorityFeeGasWeightedNumeratorWei, averageFeePriceWei,
averageTransactionFeeWei, averageTransactionGasUsed, averageTransactionInputDataSizeBytes,
averageTransactionInputDataCompressedSizeBytes, averagePriorityFeeWeightedWei,
averagePriorityFeeWei, batcherQueueSize, batcherIntensity, batcherLowerThreshold,
batcherUpperThreshold, batcherMaxBlockSize, batcherMaxTxSize
```

## `GET /blocks/:blockNumber`

Returns one compact stored block row as a JSON array using the same field order as `/blocks.names`.
Returns `404` if the block is not stored.

## `GET /block/:blockNumber`

Requires transaction data to be enabled. Returns `{ "cached": false, "block": ... }` for one stored
block plus up to 1,000 stored transactions in ascending position order. Returns `404` when
transaction data is disabled or the block is unknown.

The block includes the metrics from `/blocks` plus `blockNumberDecimal` and `transactions`.
Each transaction includes:

```txt
position, hash, from, to, type, nonce, valueWei, gasLimit, gasUsed,
inputDataSizeBytes, inputDataCompressedSizeBytes, cumulativeGasUsed, gasPriceWei,
maxFeePerGasWei, maxPriorityFeePerGasWei, effectiveGasPriceWei, priorityFeeWei,
transactionFeeWei, status, contractAddress
```

## `GET /ranges`

Returns precomputed fixed-size block range aggregate rows. Results default to `range_start`
descending and are capped at 10,000 rows. A range row exists only when the aggregator has written it.
Supported range sizes are `2`, `5`, `10`, `20`, `50`, `100`, `200`, `500`, and `1000`. Range
boundaries are `[k * M, k * M + M - 1]`.

Query parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `rangeSize` | One supported size. Defaults to `100`. |
| `rangeStartGt` | Only ranges with `range_start > rangeStartGt`. |
| `rangeStartLt` | Only ranges with `range_start < rangeStartLt`. |
| `dateGt` | Only ranges whose `max_block_date > dateGt`; value is parsed as ISO-8601. |
| `dateLt` | Only ranges whose `min_block_date < dateLt`; value is parsed as ISO-8601. |
| `limit` | Positive integer, maximum 10,000. |
| `order` | `desc` default, or `asc`. |

Response shape includes `count`, `limit`, `truncated`, `filters`, `names`, and `ranges`.

`names` field order:

```txt
rangeSize, rangeStart, rangeEnd, minBlockDate, maxBlockDate, minBaseFeeWei,
maxBaseFeeWei, averageBaseFeeWei, totalGasUsed, totalInputDataSizeBytes,
totalInputDataCompressedSizeBytes, totalMaxGas, minMaxGasInBlock, maxMaxGasInBlock,
transactionCount, totalBlockRewardWei, totalBurntFeesWei, averageBlockRewardWei,
averageBurntFeesWei, averageFeePriceWei, averageTransactionGasUsed,
averageTransactionInputDataSizeBytes, averageTransactionInputDataCompressedSizeBytes,
averagePriorityFeeWeightedWei, averagePriorityFeeWei, minBatcherQueueSize,
maxBatcherQueueSize, averageBatcherQueueSize, averageBatcherIntensity,
averageBatcherLowerThreshold, averageBatcherUpperThreshold, averageBatcherMaxBlockSize,
averageBatcherMaxTxSize
```

## `GET /transactions`

Requires transaction data to be enabled. Returns stored transaction rows ordered by block number and
transaction position. Results default to newest first and are capped at 1,000 rows per page.

Query parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `block` | Only transactions from exactly this block number. |
| `blockGt` | Only transactions with `block_number > blockGt`. |
| `blockLt` | Only transactions with `block_number < blockLt`. |
| `address` | Only transactions from this 20-byte hex sender address; normalized to lowercase. |
| `nonceGt` | Only transactions with nonce greater than this value. |
| `nonceLt` | Only transactions with nonce lower than this value. |
| `dateGt` | Only transactions in blocks newer than this ISO-8601 timestamp. |
| `dateLt` | Only transactions in blocks older than this ISO-8601 timestamp. |
| `limit` | Positive integer, maximum 1,000. |
| `page` | Positive integer page number. Defaults to `1`. |
| `order` | `desc` default, or `asc`. |

Response shape:

```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "limit": 1000,
  "truncated": false,
  "page": 1,
  "pageSize": 1000,
  "totalCount": 0,
  "totalPages": 0,
  "hasPreviousPage": false,
  "hasNextPage": false,
  "filters": {
    "block": null,
    "blockGt": null,
    "blockLt": null,
    "address": null,
    "nonceGt": null,
    "nonceLt": null,
    "dateGt": null,
    "dateLt": null
  },
  "names": ["blockNumber"],
  "transactions": []
}
```

Each transaction row is a compact JSON array of values in `names` order.

`names` field order:

```txt
blockNumber, blockNumberDecimal, blockDate, baseBlockFeeWei, position, hash, from, to, type,
nonce, valueWei, gasLimit, gasUsed, inputDataSizeBytes, inputDataCompressedSizeBytes,
cumulativeGasUsed, gasPriceWei, maxFeePerGasWei, maxPriorityFeePerGasWei, effectiveGasPriceWei,
priorityFeeWei, transactionFeeWei, status, contractAddress, operationsSummary
```

The final `operationsSummary` value is an array of `{ operation, operationType, count }` entries
when decoded Arkiv operations are stored for the transaction, and `null` otherwise.

## `GET /transaction/:hash`

Requires transaction data to be enabled. The hash must match `0x` plus 64 hex characters.

Returns `{ "transaction": ... }`. The transaction has the same stored transaction fields as
`/transactions` and always includes `operations`, an array of decoded Arkiv operation metadata. The
array is empty if no operations are stored.

Each operation includes:

```txt
opIndex, operationType, operation, entityKey, contentType, payloadSizeBytes,
attributes, expiresAtBlocks, newOwner
```

Each operation attribute includes `key`, `valueType`, `valueTypeName`, and `value`.

## `GET /entity/:entityKey`

Requires transaction data to be enabled. The entity key must match `0x` plus 64 hex characters; it
is normalized to lowercase.

Returns the most recent stored operations on that entity key (create, update, extend, transfer,
delete, expire) in chain order — ordered by block number, transaction position, and operation index
ascending — capped at the configured history limit (`ENTITY_HISTORY_LIMIT`, default 100).
`totalOperations` always carries the full stored count; `truncated` is true when older operations
were cut off, and `firstOperation` (present only then) carries the earliest stored operation so the
create stays reachable. Returns `404` when no operations are stored for the key.
Creates are linked to their entity key from the EntityCreated receipt log, so rows scanned before
that link existed may be missing from a key's history until their blocks are re-scanned.

Responses are served from a bounded in-memory cache (`ENTITY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`, default 10,000
entries; `ENTITY_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, default 64 MiB; `ENTITY_CACHE_TTL_MS`, default 5 minutes; any
set to 0 disables caching). Cached entries — including not-found results — are evicted the moment
a scanner commits new operations for the key (Postgres NOTIFY), with the TTL as a staleness
backstop, so responses can briefly trail the chain by at most the TTL if the push channel drops.

Response shape:

```json
{
  "entityKey": "0x…",
  "count": 0,
  "totalOperations": 0,
  "truncated": false,
  "names": ["blockNumber"],
  "operations": []
}
```

`count` is the number of returned operations. Each operation (and `firstOperation`, when present)
is a compact JSON array of values in `names` order; the `attributes`, `payloadReference`, and
`referenceVerification` values stay nested JSON inside the row.

`names` field order:

```txt
blockNumber, blockNumberDecimal, blockDate, position, hash, opIndex, operationType, operation,
entityKey, contentType, payloadSizeBytes, attributes, expiresAtBlocks, newOwner, isReference,
payloadReference, referenceVerification, referenceError
```

## `GET /transaction-records`

Returns top stored transaction records by category. This endpoint is routed independently of the
transaction-data feature flag but depends on stored transaction record rows.

Query parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `limit` | Positive integer, maximum 20 through the HTTP API. Defaults to 20. |

Response shape:

```json
{
  "limit": 20,
  "names": ["blockNumber"],
  "records": {
    "gas_used": [],
    "transaction_fee": [],
    "effective_fee": []
  }
}
```

Each record is a compact JSON array of values in `names` order: the `/transactions` fields
(without `operationsSummary`) plus `category`, `recordValue`, `rank`, and `recordedAt`.

## `GET /senders`

Requires transaction data to be enabled. Returns precomputed sender-address stats from
`sender_stats`, ordered by found transaction count.

Query parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `limit` | Positive integer, maximum 10,000. |
| `order` | `desc` default for most active first, or `asc`. |

The response includes `count`, `limit`, `truncated`, `filters`, `names`, and `senders`. Each
sender row is a compact JSON array of values in `names` order:

```txt
address, latestNonce, transactionCount, totalGasUsed, totalTransactionFeeWei,
totalValueWei, averageGasUsed, averageTransactionFeeWei, firstBlockNumber,
firstBlockNumberDecimal, lastBlockNumber, lastBlockNumberDecimal, firstBlockDate,
lastBlockDate, aggregatedAt
```

## `GET /balances`

Account balance readings taken from the node, one per (block, address) where that address sent or
received a transaction in that block. Never derived from transaction values -- balances also move
through contract-internal transfers and fee payments the transaction list does not show, and the
index has no genesis anchor. Requires `SCANNER_TRACK_BALANCES=true`; never backfilled, so coverage
starts where it was switched on, and the series is sparse.

Query parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `block` | Exactly one block: the "who held what at block N" view. |
| `address` | One account's history; 20-byte hex, matched case-insensitively. |
| `blockGt`, `blockLt` | Exclusive block bounds. |
| `limit` | Positive integer, maximum 10,000. |
| `order` | `desc` default (newest block first), or `asc`. |

The response includes `count`, `limit`, `truncated`, `filters`, `names`, and `balances`. Each
balance row is a compact JSON array of values in `names` order:

```txt
blockNumber, blockDate, address, balanceWei
```

## `GET /guzzlers`

Requires Redis-backed guzzler tracking. Returns cached active-sender leaderboards computed by the
near-head scanner. The backend slices the cached board; it does not rebuild leaderboards on request.
Before the first refresh, it returns empty boards. Disabled guzzlers return `503`.

Query parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `limit` | Positive integer, maximum 250. Defaults to 100. |
| `window` | Optional single window label. One of `5m`, `20m`, `1h`, `6h`, `24h`. |

Response fields:

- `generatedAt`: board generation time.
- `retentionMs`: bucket retention period, equal to 24 hours.
- `limit`: effective top-N per window.
- `names`: compact stat field order.
- `windows`: array of requested or all windows.

`names` field order for each guzzler stat:

```txt
address, transactionCount, totalGasUsed, totalFeeWei, firstSeen, lastSeen
```

Each window row includes `label`, `windowMs`, `count`, and compact `guzzlers` rows.

## `GET /guzzler/:address`

Requires Redis-backed guzzler tracking. The address must be a 20-byte hex address and is normalized
to lowercase. Returns one sender's retained one-minute history over the 24-hour retention window. An
unknown sender returns an empty history.

Response fields include:

```txt
address, generatedAt, retentionMs, bucketMs, count, names, points
```

`names` field order for each point:

```txt
minute, startTime, transactionCount, totalGasUsed, totalFeeWei, firstSeen, lastSeen
```

## Baseload APIs

Baseload is a backend control plane for Arkiv load-generation workers. The browser never sends
private-key material or Arkiv RPC calls directly. The backend derives worker wallets from the
configured mnemonic at `m/44'/60'/0'/0/<walletNumber>`.

Worker config version is `2`. Worker behavior values:

```txt
create, create-update, create-ownership, time-bomb, create-update-delete
```

Worker config fields:

```txt
id, behavior, maxGasPriceGwei, opsPerMinute, entitiesPerRequest, singleCreatePayloadSize,
singleCreateStringArgumentCount, singleCreateNumberArgumentCount, entityPoolSize,
timeBombOffsetSeconds, walletNumber, walletAddress, startBlock, endBlock,
durationSeconds, ttlSeconds
```

`entitiesPerRequest` is normalized to at most `1`; use `opsPerMinute` or multiple worker
wallets to scale load instead of multi-entity mutation batches.

### `GET /baseload`

Returns backend Baseload state, enabled/runtime availability, active config, and worker statuses.
This route is public even when `BASELOAD_ADMIN_BEARER_TOKEN` is configured.

### `PUT /baseload`

Replaces the active backend Baseload config and starts, updates, or stops workers to match it.
Requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when `BASELOAD_ADMIN_BEARER_TOKEN` is set. The request body
must be a JSON object normalizable to:

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "workers": []
}
```

Invalid JSON or invalid config returns `400`. If no admin token is configured, mutation is
unrestricted.

### `GET /admin/verify`

Validates the configured Baseload admin bearer token. Returns `503` when no admin bearer token is
configured. Requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and returns `{ "authorized": true }` on success.

### Saved Baseload Configs

All saved config routes require the admin bearer token when `BASELOAD_ADMIN_BEARER_TOKEN` is set.
Names are URL-decoded, trimmed, must start with a letter or number, may contain letters, numbers,
spaces, dots, underscores, or hyphens, and are limited to 80 characters.

| Method | Path | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/baseload/configs` | Returns `{ "configs": [...] }` with `name`, `workerCount`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. |
| `GET` | `/baseload/configs/:name` | Returns one saved config summary plus `config`. |
| `PUT` | `/baseload/configs/:name` | Saves a normalized config body under the name. |
| `DELETE` | `/baseload/configs/:name` | Deletes the named config and returns `{ "deleted": true|false }`. |
| `PUT` | `/baseload/configs/:name/load` | Loads the saved config into the active Baseload runtime. Returns `503` if runtime is unavailable. |

## Stored Metric Conventions

- `baseBlockFeeWei` comes from block `baseFeePerGas`; networks without it store `0`.
- `maxGasInBlock` is block `gasLimit`.
- Transaction fee is `receipt.gasUsed * receipt.effectiveGasPrice`.
- Priority fee is `max(effectiveGasPrice - baseFeePerGas, 0)`.
- `averageFeePriceWei` is the simple per-transaction average of `effectiveGasPrice`.
- `averageTransactionGasUsed` is the simple per-transaction average of receipt gas used.
- `averagePriorityFeeWeightedWei` is weighted by receipt gas used.
- Empty blocks store `0` for average values.
- Batcher collector fields are nullable enrichment metrics:
  `batcherQueueSize`, `batcherIntensity`, `batcherLowerThreshold`, `batcherUpperThreshold`,
  `batcherMaxBlockSize`, `batcherMaxTxSize`.

## Arkiv Operation Metadata

The scanner can send Arkiv registry transaction calldata to the external decoder service. A decoder
HTTP 400 means the calldata is not an Arkiv `execute()` call and is skipped. Other decoder failures
make the whole block retry.

Stored operation metadata is keyed by transaction block number, position, and operation index.
Stored fields include operation type/name, entity key, content type, attributes, expiry, new owner,
and `payloadSizeBytes`.

Never expect `payload.hex`, `payload.text`, or raw transaction `input` in database rows or API
responses. They are intentionally dropped and must not be persisted.

## Scanner and Aggregator Behavior Relevant to API Data

- The scanner stores one completed block at a time and resumes from the last successfully stored
  block.
- A failed block read is retried and is not skipped.
- The block row, transaction rows, operation rows, and scanner progress update are written in one
  PostgreSQL transaction.
- The main range aggregator writes `block_ranges` for complete fixed-size windows only.
- `aggregate-all` walks every supported range size repeatedly.
- `aggregate-senders` rebuilds `sender_stats` from stored transaction rows.
- The guzzler cache is database-free recent activity in Redis. It keeps one-minute buckets for 24
  hours and cached top-N boards for the configured windows.

## Frontend Notes for API Consumers

- Development frontend uses Vite and proxies `/api` to the backend.
- Production frontend uses `frontend/server.js` to serve static files and reverse-proxy `/api/*`.
- Direct backend URLs use paths such as `/blocks`; frontend-origin URLs use `/api/blocks`.
- Readonly views and status APIs are public. Baseload mutating controls send the optional admin
  bearer token from browser local storage only when configured by the user.
- The `/data` page reads live entity state over JSON-RPC, not from the index. It takes an Arkiv 0.8 query
  (`arkiv_query` with every projection except the payload; page sizes 5–100, node cap 200) and records each
  run in the URL as `q`, `pageSize` (default 25) and `expiration` (`all` | `soon`, a client-side 24h filter
  estimated from `arkiv_getBlockTiming`), so `/data?q=%24owner+%3D+addr(0x..)` is a shareable link that runs
  on load. A bare 64-hex key or 40-hex address in `q` is rewritten to `$key = key(..)` / `$owner = addr(..)`.
  Paging resumes the node cursor at the block the first page was read at. By default it POSTs to
  `/api/shadow-rpc`, so the backend must forward `arkiv_query`, `arkiv_getEntityCount` and
  `arkiv_getBlockTiming` (the default `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM_METHODS` once `SHADOW_RPC_UPSTREAM` is set). The
  page can be switched to a custom RPC URL called directly from the browser; that endpoint must allow
  cross-origin requests. Its "Check connection" probe issues `eth_chainId`, `web3_clientVersion` and the three
  Arkiv reads and never writes.
